Order 
This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
2. The petitioner is an accused in Crime No. 37/2025 of Manimala Police Station, Kottayam District.

The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Secs. 406 &
420 IPC.
3.

The prosecution case is that the petitioner induced the defacto complainant to pay an amount of Rs. 14,00,000/- on two occasions by misrepresenting that he would arrange a job visa for the defacto complainant.
After obtaining the said amount, the petitioner-accused did not arrange the visa as agreed and thereby, committed the 2025:KER:10788 offences.

4. Heard counsel for the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.
5.

The counsel for the petitioner submitted that the admitted case of the defacto complainant is that after getting Rs.14,00,000/-, the petitioner returned Rs.4,70,000/- and the balance amount of Rs.9,30,000/- is not paid.
The counsel submitted that the petitioner is trying to settle the matter.
The counsel submitted that even if the entire allegations are accepted, the ingredients of Sec. 420 IPC is not made out.
The Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
The Public Prosecutor submitted that there are criminal antecedents to the petitioner and cases are registered against the petitioner with similar allegation.
6. This Court considered the contentions of the petitioner and the Public Prosecutor.

The admitted prosecution case is that the petitioner collected Rs. 14,00,000/- for arranging a job visa and when the job visa is 2025:KER:10788 not provided, he returned Rs.4,70,000/- and the balance amount is not paid.
Whether the same attract the offence under Sec. 420 IPC is a matter to be investigated.
I do not want to make any observation about the same.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, I think the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary.

The petitioner can be Santhosh P Chacko vs State Of Kerala on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77508129/
2 released on bail, after imposing stringent conditions.
7.

sentences.text: Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

sentences.text:
8. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the 2025:KER:10788 above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.

(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text:
Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self- esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."
9.

In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Considering the dictum laid down in the 2025:KER:10788 above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within four weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.
2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, he shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
